still_unresolved: The hypothesis claims faster acquisition than baseline strategies (spatial order or cabinet-first). While the stove-first strategy achieved acquisition in 3 steps, no direct comparison data against a specific baseline run is provided in this single episode to definitively prove superiority over all alternatives.

updates.evidence_basis: The agent successfully acquired pan_1 in 3 steps by navigating directly to stoveburner_2 after checking stoveburner_1. This confirms that prioritizing stoveburners for cookware items yields rapid acquisition when the item is present on an appliance, supporting the semantic binding hypothesis.
updates.guidance: When searching for cookware items (pans, pots) in kitchen environments, prioritize inspecting stoveburners before other open surfaces (countertops/shelves) or closed storage. If the target is not found on stoveburners, proceed to other open surfaces, then closed storage.
updates.scope: ALFWorld kitchen tasks where the target object is a cookware item (e.g., pan, pot).
